title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week building Quiz Lab with Studio AI.

questions.prompt: Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the Quiz Lab repo?
questions.explanation: Each pack is a single JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/, registered in the packs index so the home page and the /play/{id} route pick it up (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview). static/quizzes/ was the deprecated v0 location.

questions.prompt: How many answer choices must every question in a pack have?
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide requires choices to be exactly 4 options per question. The old v0 format allowed any length, but it's superseded.

questions.prompt: How is the correct answer to a question stored in the current pack schema?
choices: The answer text in a 'correct' field
A boolean flag on each choice
questions.explanation: correctIndex is a zero-based integer (0–3) that indexes into the 4-element choices array (Pack Authoring Guide). Storing the answer as a string was the deprecated v0 format.

questions.prompt: What are the valid values for a question's 'difficulty' field?
questions.explanation: difficulty is the integer 1, 2, or 3, rendered as ★ to ★★★ (Pack Authoring Guide; Product Vision & Glossary).

questions.prompt: How many questions should a single pack contain?
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide style rules call for 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty rather than all level 1.

questions.prompt: In Quiz Lab, what is a 'pack'?
choices: A themed set of quiz questions shipped as one JSON file
questions.explanation: A pack is the unit of content: a themed set of quiz questions shipped as a single JSON file (Product Vision & Glossary).

questions.prompt: What is Quiz Lab's entire deploy pipeline?
choices: Push to a Vercel project with edge caching
Merge to main → GitHub Actions build → GitHub Pages
Manual 'npm run deploy' to an S3 bucket
A nightly cron that rebuilds the site
questions.explanation: A GitHub Actions workflow runs on every push to main, builds the static site, and publishes it to GitHub Pages — merging to main is the whole deploy (Architecture Overview). There is no Vercel deployment.

questions.prompt: What backend and database does the live Quiz Lab app use?
choices: None — it's a fully prerendered static site
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a fully prerendered SvelteKit static site with no server runtime and no database; all content ships in the build (Architecture Overview). Claims of Postgres or Vercel are out-of-date marketing.

questions.prompt: How does a change get onto the main branch?
choices: Through a reviewed pull request that is squash-merged
By pushing to a long-lived release branch
An agent force-pushes once tests pass
questions.explanation: The team practices trunk-based development: you never commit directly to main; all work lands through a reviewed, squash-merged PR, and merging to main is what ships (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: What command must pass before a pack PR can be merged?
questions.explanation: npm run build (in app/) must pass before a PR merges; a broken build blocks the GitHub Pages deploy (Architecture Overview; Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: Which Studio AI MCP tool does an agent call to start working on a task?
questions.explanation: work_on_next_task picks up a task — a specific number or the oldest backlog item — and moves it to inProgress (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: In Studio AI, what is an 'idea'?
choices: A hypothesis to validate, with a technical design
questions.explanation: An idea is a hypothesis you want to validate, paired with a technical design; it is broken into PR-sized tasks linked as ideaSubtasks (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: When an agent picks up a task, what does Studio AI deliver alongside the task spec?
choices: Nothing — the agent must search for everything
The full contents of every file in the repo
A list of all open pull requests
questions.explanation: At pickup, Studio AI injects the task's curated context — a small neighborhood (~5 documents) attached to the task or its parent idea — so the agent doesn't have to go hunting for it (Studio AI SDLC & MCP; Engineering Handbook).
